kept.name: kb
kept.reason: Appears to be your own system (typed wiki records, deterministic graph, full-text search). It's the baseline the other results should be compared against.

kept.name: gbrain
kept.reason: Prior catalog decision about this exact question: kb already covers typed links and search, and vector embeddings should be added to the existing index rather than adopting a separate system.

kept.name: claude-mem
kept.reason: Skipped because kb covered the need. Records why a SQLite, Chroma and worker-service vector stack was judged not worth it, and notes its 3-layer progressive-disclosure retrieval.

kept.name: okf-agent-memory
kept.reason: Very close match: git-native Markdown+YAML knowledge for coding agents with in-memory BM25 over MCP. A reviewer flagged that it publishes no recall or precision numbers, a lesson that applies to you too.

kept.name: three-store-hybrid-memory-architecture
kept.reason: Argues that agent memory needs vector, exact-lookup and graph stores merged by a fusion layer. Maps directly onto your lexical + graph + embeddings design.

kept.name: titans-atlas-cronus
kept.reason: Atlas is local project memory that combines lexical, vector, graph and evidence/provenance retrieval and explicitly refuses to treat vector search alone as memory. Close in spirit to your approach.

kept.name: memoose
kept.reason: Local coding-agent memory on a deterministic SQLite knowledge graph, with an optional fastembed extra for local embeddings and evidence pointers on facts. A close comparable.

kept.name: tencentdb-agent-memory
kept.reason: Agent memory with typed assets and link-graphed wiki pages, retrieved by BM25 + vector + RRF under budget caps. A concrete hybrid design to compare against.

kept.name: tolvi
kept.reason: Markdown+YAML decision vault for coding agents with a CAG mode (load the whole vault) and a pgvector RAG mode. Useful for the CAG-vs-RAG tradeoff on a small corpus.

kept.name: mempalace
kept.reason: Local agent memory with published benchmarks: 96.6% R@5 with semantic search alone, 98.4% with keyword-boosting hybrid heuristics. Gives you a measured reference for how much hybrid adds.

kept.name: synapse-memory-layer
kept.reason: Memory system with typed atoms plus immutable evidence signals and atom links in pgvector. Its write-quality and critic pipeline is a comparable design.

kept.name: ai-memory-comparison
kept.reason: Source-backed survey of 73 coding-agent memory systems across 79 features, including search and retrieval. Useful for placing your system among the alternatives.

kept.name: contextual-retrieval-anthropic
kept.reason: The standard hybrid recipe: contextual embeddings + BM25 fused with weighted RRF + reranking, with measured gains at each step.

kept.name: sira-superintelligent-retrieval-agent
kept.reason: Shows that well-enriched lexical BM25 (offline vocabulary enrichment plus IDF-checked query expansion) can beat dense retrieval. A strong case for your lexical-first base.

kept.name: agentic-rag-terminal-tools
kept.reason: Evidence that agents using grep beat embedding retrieval, and that Claude Code dropped vector search. A counterpoint to weigh before investing heavily in embeddings.

kept.name: rag-architecture-decision-tree
kept.reason: Diagnostic framework: add hybrid, graph or reranking only to fix an observed failure, and measure retrieval separately from generation.

kept.name: rag-retrieval-recipe
kept.reason: Practitioner baseline: local embedding models, embed once and re-run only on change, over-retrieve then rerank, and require citations.

kept.name: production-rag-system-taxonomy
kept.reason: Checklist of production concerns, such as freshness, evals and observability, to check your system against.

kept.name: graphrag-agent-memory-linkedin-series
kept.reason: Conceptual grounding for knowledge-graph-backed agent memory, plus a rule of thumb for when graph retrieval beats plain RAG.

kept.name: fluxmem
kept.reason: Graph memory with typed semantic, episodic and procedural nodes, plus link expansion and pruning driven by retrieval feedback. Ideas you could apply to a linked record graph.

kept.name: iai-personal-memory-engine
kept.reason: Local memory that keeps a vector index and a graph in one store with a small local embedder (bge-small). A comparable architecture.

kept.name: agent-dispatcher
kept.reason: Retrieval for coding agents built on multiple signals rather than embeddings first, and it runs semantic memory in shadow mode before letting it change rankings. A good rollout pattern for your embeddings.

kept.name: skill-search-mcp
kept.reason: Small-corpus semantic search for Claude Code using embedded Qdrant + fastembed with no external service, plus content-hash incremental reindexing and a recall eval harness.

kept.name: pdf-mcp
kept.reason: MCP server doing BM25 + semantic search fused with RRF, with section-aware chunking and a SQLite cache. A compact local hybrid implementation to compare with.

kept.name: agentic-rag
kept.reason: Agent reformulates queries and retrieves over several rounds. Relevant to how agents will call your search tool.

kept.name: pageindex
kept.reason: Vectorless alternative: LLM reasoning over a hierarchical tree index. Comparable to navigating a structured graph instead of using embeddings.

kept.name: chromadb
kept.reason: Embeddable local store that combines dense, BM25/sparse and metadata filtering in one query. A candidate backend for adding embeddings.

kept.name: lancedb
kept.reason: In-process embedded vector + BM25 hybrid store with no server. Suits a lightweight local system.

kept.name: qdrant
kept.reason: Hybrid dense/sparse search with RRF/DBSF fusion and an in-process Edge variant. A candidate backend.

kept.name: weaviate
kept.reason: BM25 + vector hybrid with an alpha weighting parameter. A reference for how fusion weights are exposed.

kept.name: pgvector
kept.reason: Shows hybrid search done by fusing Postgres full-text and vector results with RRF. An option if your records live in SQL.

kept.name: onyx-ai-platform
kept.reason: Reference architecture for agentic RAG over a hybrid vector + BM25 index with reranking.

kept.name: five-levels-of-chunking
kept.reason: Chunking taxonomy. Structure-based chunking applies to embedding typed markdown records.

kept.name: vector-distance-metrics-cheatsheet
kept.reason: Practical embedding choices: picking the right distance metric and using Matryoshka truncation to cut vector size.

kept.name: ann-index-methods
kept.reason: Notes that exact flat search is best below about 100K vectors, so a small record corpus likely doesn't need an ANN index.

kept.name: isaacflath-ocr-guides
kept.reason: Its retrieval posts cover BM25, dense/ColBERT retrieval, late chunking and reranking, based on production experience.

kept.name: understand-anything
kept.reason: Combines deterministic tree-sitter graph edges with LLM semantic annotations and search, and includes a wiki knowledge-graph mode. Parallels your deterministic graph plus semantics.
